Amenda Demo Runbook

Every screenshot below is the real app, captured from a live sweep against the PivotStack file. Left column is what you say; right column is what the judges see.

4:30Target runtime

Before you stand up

  • Start the backend from amenda/backend: python -m uvicorn main:app --port 8000, then open 127.0.0.1:8000.
  • Run python demo/preflight.py. It checks the key, the server, the demo data and the live scrape, and resets the redline to “pending” if you rehearsed. It makes no LLM calls, so it costs nothing and you can run it as many times as you like. If it prints Ready to present, you are done — everything below is what it checks for you.
  • Never press Select all before sweeping — that is 7 amendments × 7 clients. The flow below sweeps one amendment, which is 7 calls and about 20 seconds.

If pre-flight reports a problem: a missing .env stops the sweep entirely (it is gitignored, so a fresh clone never has it); a failed live scrape is harmless — the cached snapshot loads automatically, just say “cached snapshot” rather than “live” if a judge asks.

01

Open cold on the dashboard

0:20

Script: “Judges, we present to you Amenda… an early warning safeguard for lawyer-client documents.”

Say

“Judges, we present Amenda. Amenda is an early warning safeguard for lawyer–client documents that are at risk from amendments moving through Parliament.”

“Horizon scanning tells you the law changed. Amenda tells you which of your clients' documents are now wrong, why, and what to do.”

  • Don't click anything yet. Let the header read: seven clients, twenty-one documents.
  • The right panel is the statute book; the centre is where you ask questions.
02

Feature 1 — the bill, read for you

1:00

Script: “Amendment bills go up to 200 pages… Amenda's first feature reduces the time lawyers need to parse the bill” — purpose plus up-to-3 high-impact sections, drawn only from the Explanatory Notes.

Say

“This is the Workplace Fairness Act 2024, Bill 50 of 2024. Passed 8 January 2025, expected in force 2026 to 2027 — that gap is exactly where Amenda earns its place.”

“An amendment bill runs to 200 pages, most of it definitions and consequential drafting. Amenda gives two things: the legislative purpose, and the high-impact sections. Both drawn only from the Explanatory Notes — that is how we keep it from hallucinating.”

“Section 7: no employment decision on a protected characteristic, including age. Section 41: any term that blocks a grievance is void.”

  • Click Before / after on the Workplace Fairness Act card.
  • Scroll the dialog once so Main provisions comes into view.
03

The three stages, and the honest gap

0:35

Script: “real-time data on bills at the 3 main stages. First reading, second reading, and when the amendment has come into effect.”

Say

“Amenda tracks bills at three stages — first reading, second reading, and commencement. These are scraped live from parliament.gov.sg, and each bill's PDF is parsed for its commencement clause.”

“Note the third chip: commencement not stated — Minister to appoint. When the Minister has given no date, we say so rather than guessing. A tool that invents a date is worse than no tool.”

  • Close the dialog, click the Watchlist tab.
  • Then click back to Confirmed before step 4.
04

Feature 2 — the sweep, and Chen Wei

1:10

Script: “Meet Chen Wei, founder of a 30-person tech startup… contracts sitting in the file, ready to be sent to three new hires next week.” Tell the story while it runs — the wait becomes the setup.

Say

“With the amendment selected, I run the sweep across every client on file.” (press Run sweep on selected)

“While that runs — meet Chen Wei. Founder of PivotStack, a 30-person tech startup. His firm drafted employment contracts eighteen months ago on his instruction: one clause terminating employment automatically at 62, another waiving the right to raise grievances.”

“Those contracts are sitting in the firm's file, ready to go out to three new hires next week.”

  • Press Run sweep on selected — the status line names the real workload.
  • Do not fill the silence with apology. The story is exactly as long as the sweep.
05

Two exposures, two different ways of finding them

0:50

Script: “flags out documents that contain clauses that are potentially affected… classified into two categories of risk” — plus your Q&A answer on how risk is graded.

Say

“Two exposures, found two different ways. PivotStack is caught in the document — clause 8.3 quoted verbatim, marked ‘found in text’. Every flag carries the actual words, so the lawyer verifies rather than trusts.”

“Kallang Works is caught by profile — forty employees, no grievance procedure, and no document on file mentions one. The exposure exists precisely because nothing was written down.”

“And at the bottom: twenty documents scanned and left unflagged. Topical overlap is not impact. A tool that flags everything has told you nothing.”

  • Read the Why line aloud — it names Ground 1 (timing) and Ground 2 (operative vs subsidiary clause).
  • That is your risk-grading answer, already on screen.
06

The redline — both clauses, one diff

0:50

Script: “Amenda has a redline/tracked changes feature… User simply chooses to approve or reject.”

Say

“Amenda proposes the edit.” (press Propose the edit) “Red is struck out, green is inserted — the format every lawyer in this room already reads.”

“Clause 8.3's age trigger is gone, replaced with a performance review anchored to the Retirement and Re-employment Act. Clause 14.1 flips from a void waiver into a compliant grievance process.”

“Underneath: what changed, and what it costs to leave it — fifty thousand dollars per breach. And a Judgement line naming what still needs the lawyer's call. Amenda does not pretend that part is automatable.”

  • Scroll so Change, If left and Judgement are all visible.
  • The Judgement row is your credibility moment — it admits a limit.
07

Approve — and the record that follows

0:45

Script: “suggested legally compliant replacements for the lawyer to approve in one click.” This is also your liability answer, shown rather than argued.

Say

“The lawyer approves.” (press Approve, then Audit trail) “And the decision is on the record — who decided, when, and the provision that compelled it.”

“Amenda never edits a document on its own. Every change is approved, rejected or flagged by a named lawyer. This is the log a firm shows its insurer.”

“Amenda is a drafting aid, not counsel. It sits where a junior associate sits — the approving solicitor keeps full professional responsibility, exactly as they always have.”

  • Press Approve, then Audit trail in the header.
  • Close on the audit dialog open — it is the strongest last frame you have.
08

If you have thirty seconds spare

0:20

Script: “scans existing client database of both the client's personal profile, employment contracts as well as their corporate constitution.”

Say

“This is the client file Amenda reads — profile, contracts, corporate constitution. Documents can be uploaded straight in; the text is extracted and swept like any other.”

“The constitution was scanned and left clean. Only the employment contract was wrong.”

  • Click PivotStack Pte Ltd in the sidebar.
  • Cut this beat first if you are running long — steps 1–7 are the demo.

Q&A — your answers, and where they live on screen

Every one of these can be answered by pointing at something you have already shown. Re-open the screen rather than describing it.

What if the parliamentary site changes structure?

The scrapers sit behind one parser interface, so a layout change is a contained edit rather than a rewrite. Sources are all public government domains — Parliament, eGazette, SSO.

Show: the Watchlist tab, “PDF parsed ✓”.

High risk or moderate — how do you decide?

Two grounds. Timing: a bill still at first reading caps at moderate, because the firm cannot yet be wrong about a rule that is not law. Clause hierarchy: the operative clause that states the outdated position is high; a clause exposed only by reference is moderate.

Show: the Why line in step 5 — it names both grounds.

Who is the customer — the firm or the client?

The firm. Amenda sits inside the firm's workflow; the lawyer remains the professional who advises. That also keeps us the right side of the legal-advice boundary.

Show: the approve/reject controls — a lawyer stands between the tool and the client.

What stops a lawyer approving everything unread?

Nothing stops a careless lawyer — that is equally true of the precedent templates firms use today. Amenda is positioned as a junior associate's suggestion: the approving solicitor keeps full professional responsibility. The difference is that here the suggestion carries its authority and a verbatim quote, so checking it is faster than ignoring it.

Show: the audit trail — every decision is attributed.

Where is client data stored?

On the firm's own infrastructure. Bring-your-own-environment: Amenda integrates with the firm's existing document management system, so no client data leaves it. Consistent with enterprise legal tech and with PDPA obligations.

Note: the demo corpus is synthetic — say so plainly.

How do you know it isn't hallucinating?

Three constraints. Bill summaries come only from the Explanatory Statement. Every flag carries a verbatim quote from the document, marked found or inferred. And the engine is scored against hand-labelled ground truth — precision, recall, and deliberate false-positive traps.

Show: “20 documents scanned and left unflagged”. Or run: python backend/eval.py
Client corpus is synthetic — no real client data. Regulatory sources are real. Screenshots captured from a live sweep, 6 September 2026.
